title: playable-screen-20of44
queue_order: One binary (this lane's step-1 commit, merged with origin/master), env-only A/B per title: ON queues with no --env (app default); OFF queues --env with all six vars =0. Scope at first registration: 20 of pm/playable-accepted.tsv's 44 titles whose ISO was present on the Nova's DEVICE_ISO_ROOT (confirmed against /home/justin/hakux-work/hardware/titlepush/listing-nova.txt, Oct-3, cross-checked live at queue time). lane.local's brief addendum (10-10 22:46 PDT) added Capcom vs. SNK 2 EO and shuffled 23 more titles onto the Nova overnight (unit lanelocal-shuffle1010b, log /home/justin/hakux-work/lanelocal-scratch/shuffle1010.log, done 23:43:58 PDT). The pilot (Alien Hominid) then failed live with 'title not on device' despite being in the original 20 -- cross-checking wt/pathfind/scratch/nova-free1008.log (an Oct-8 21:25-21:49 PDT space-freeing pass this lane had not seen) against tonight's 23 restored titles found 12 titles deleted Oct-8 and never restored: Alien Hominid, KOF: Maximum Impact - Maniax, Azurik: Rise of Perathia, WWE Raw 2, 50 Cent: Bulletproof, Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance, Kabuki Warriors, 187: Ride or Die, Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2x, Gunvalkyrie, Castlevania: Curse of Darkness, NBA Live 2004. These move to blocked_titles; the true current scope is 32 (9 of the original 20 unaffected by the Oct-8 deletion, plus Capcom vs. SNK 2 EO, plus the 23 restored tonight). 14 of the 32 use their own named route (docs/testing/titles/routes/<name>.route, minus the five route-having titles now blocked: alien-hominid, 187-ride-or-die, kabuki-warriors, thps2x, castlevania-cod -- 4 route titles remain: Crimson Skies, Spikeout, Jet Set Radio Future, Tork); the rest run as a soak to the title screen with --frames-every. Queued in batches of about 10 titles, each batch preceded by its own small pilot per the 30-min device-time gate, HAKUX_RELEASE_PRIO=1. gfps for a route run is read from hakuX-pace logcat lines (f=... vb=... max=... ms=...) summed across the window from 'mark gameplay' to 'soak end': gfps = sum(vb)*1000/sum(ms), the same vsync-paced-frame count raread.py/fpread.py already parse for NFS, generalized here without the NFS-specific race-start countdown windowing (most titles have no discrete race start). Crimson Skies pilot (first of this batch, refs 1-1791703775-fastpaths1010-4011126 ON / -4011199 OFF): both arms clean (env correct, all four on-lines present on ON and absent on OFF, no fatal/crash/abort, golden disk state both arms), gfps ON 59.90 OFF 59.94 -- no regression, this title is not bottlenecked by the six switches either way.
judge: per-title: logcat read for a crash/hang/abort in ON that OFF does not show (fatal); route-frames or --frames-every captures at matched points, compared by region, ON vs OFF (frames); reportasync1010's armed/late counters where GET_REPORT traffic appears in logcat (reports); both arms' perf_regimen.json/telemetry fps, reported not gated (gfps). No single numeric threshold applies across 20 different titles -- each title's own row is read by eye against its own OFF baseline, recorded in docs/lanes/fastpaths1010/NOTES.md and PR.md's screen table.
baseline: Every one of the 20 titles already has an accepted Playable verdict (pm/playable-accepted.tsv) from an earlier run, most on this same Nova, establishing what correct gameplay for that title's route looks like; this screen's OFF arm is that same known-good code path (all six switches at their native C default, off), and ON is the new default. A title regressing between ON and OFF here would be a regression from fastpaths1010's own step-1 commit, not a pre-existing issue the Playable verdict already accepted.
prediction: None of the 44 fail: reportasync1010, texscan1010 (paired with REPORT_ASYNC), drawrec1010 and perdrawon1010 each already screened their own switch (or pair) on some subset of Playable titles or a broader survey without a correctness regression (texscan1010's own finding was a PERFORMANCE regression when TEXSCAN runs alone, not a correctness one, and this toggle never ships TEXSCAN alone). What would refute it: any ON-only crash/hang; any ON-only visual defect in a frame region OFF does not show; a title whose reportasync counters show armed below 100% that OFF's do not (a GET_REPORT race the other three lanes' own survey titles did not happen to hit).
expect_note: fail_titles starts empty: the claim under test is that no SCOPED title fails. blocked_titles started as 24 titles not yet on the Nova (this lane's Oct-3/4 listing check was stale by one: Capcom vs. SNK 2 EO was already there), which lane.local's addendum (10-10 22:46 PDT) shuffled on overnight (lanelocal-shuffle1010b, log /home/justin/hakux-work/lanelocal-scratch/shuffle1010.log, done 23:43:58 PDT, all 23 verified). The Alien Hominid pilot then failed live with 'title not on device' -- cross-checking wt/pathfind/scratch/nova-free1008.log (an Oct-8 21:25-21:49 PDT space-freeing pass not previously seen) found it deleted that day and never restored, along with 11 others from the original 20 that tonight's shuffle didn't touch (it only restored the 23 named in the brief addendum). Those 12 are blocked_titles now. The current 32-title scope: 8 of the original 20 the Oct-8 deletion did not touch (Crimson Skies: High Road to Revenge, ToeJam & Earl III: Mission to Earth, Spikeout: Battle Street, Halo: Combat Evolved, Panzer Dragoon Orta, Jet Set Radio Future, Tork: Prehistoric Punk, Call of Duty 3), Capcom vs. SNK 2 EO, and the 23 restored tonight. Full per-title list, route/soak plan and the presence correction: docs/lanes/fastpaths1010/NOTES.md section 4.1.2.
